drivingQuestion: Why is the placenta of a consecrated animal presumed to have come from a sacred fetus, so that it must be buried?
outcomeNote: The mishna's distinction between firstborn and other consecrated animals is grounded in the different scope of sanctity.

segments.he: וּבַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין תִּקָּבֵר. מַאי טַעְמָא? רוּבָּא בַּר מִיקְדָּשׁ הוּא.
segments.en: § The continuation of the mishna states: «But in» the case of «sacrificial» animals the placenta «must be buried,» because it came from a fetus that is assumed to have been sacred. The Gemara asks: «What is the reason» to assume this? The Gemara answers: It is because the «majority» of the offspring of sacrificial animals «are fit to be sacred,» as, in contrast to firstborn status, both female and male offspring of sacrificial animals can be sacred. Therefore, one must be concerned that the offspring, and its placenta, were sacred.
